explanation: Its neighbours, Switzerland and Austria, have no coast either, so reaching the sea means crossing at least two borders. Uzbekistan is the world's only other doubly landlocked country.

claims.text: Liechtenstein is landlocked, and its only neighbours, Switzerland and Austria, are landlocked too.
Luxembourg borders Belgium, France and Germany, Andorra borders France and Spain, and San Marino borders Italy, and all of those neighbours have a sea coast.
Travelling from Liechtenstein to the sea means crossing at least two international borders.
Liechtenstein and Uzbekistan are the only two doubly landlocked countries.

writerNotes: Self-check (§9.3). Lint: content:check reports no errors or warnings for this item. Claims: every checkable statement is listed; c1 and c4 are high under the C26 floor ('only'), c3 for its number; c2 is a plain border fact. Datasets: mledoze-countries cca3=LIE borders AUT, CHE and landlocked true; AUT and CHE landlocked true; LUX borders BEL, FRA, DEU; AND borders FRA, ESP; SMR borders ITA. For c4 I filtered the file for landlocked entries whose every neighbour is also landlocked: it returns LIE and UZB only (UZB borders AFG, KAZ, KGZ, TJK, TKM). c3 follows from c1. Rival test: Luxembourg pulls hardest (small, landlocked, wedged between big neighbours), but Belgium, France and Germany all have coasts; Andorra and San Marino fail the same way. Against the key: the Rhine gives Liechtenstein a river route to the North Sea, but a river is not a coast, so the key stands. Volatility: evergreen, settled geography with no review date; no time words, and nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026. Regional: a European subject, but the reasoning needs only a mental map, so players anywhere can work it out option by option. Style: Oxford spelling, plain hyphens only, straight quotes, explanation of 28 words. Myths: every claim screened against content/reference/myths.json; no match. Mystery and encore: nothing of either kind to check in a practice item. Doubts: c4 treats the Caspian as a lake, so Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan count as landlocked; that is the usual convention and the dataset's own flag. Seeded 5 because few players know the term, though a good reasoner can test each option's neighbours.

stem: Which European country is doubly landlocked, with only landlocked countries as its neighbours?
